question: During natural family planning, what does a woman look for when checking her cervical mucus for peak fertility?

options.A: A thick, sticky discharge that remains present all month
options.B: A brownish bloody discharge right before ovulation
options.C: Complete dryness with no vaginal secretions at all
options.D: Clear, stretchy mucus that looks like raw egg white

question: What major problem in Nigerian healthcare do HMO payment systems try to solve?

question: What happens to the price of a food item when its supply drops sharply while consumer demand remains the same?

question: Why do elderly parents in some communities heavily rely on having sons to take care of them in old age?

options.B: Higher wages earned exclusively by male workers

options.D: Mandatory retirement funds managed by community elders

question: At what point should a sharps disposal container be closed and replaced to keep everyone safe?

question: Which process is required to make surgical tools safe if they will enter sterile body tissues?

question: Why must a nurse monitor a child closely while they receive rapid IV fluids?

question: Which pillar of safe motherhood focuses on checking on the mother and baby right after childbirth?

options.A: Family planning

question: Why is talking about food such a powerful tool when nursing patients with chronic illnesses?

options.A: Dietary changes directly influence disease progression and symptoms

options.C: It completely replaces the need for prescribed medications
options.D: It lowers the patient's hospital utility bills

question: Before you start draining an uncomfortable abscess, what piece of patient history is most crucial to check?

options.A: Blood type classification
options.B: Recent dietary preferences
options.C: Allergies to local anesthetics
options.D: History of childhood asthma

question: Why is occupational therapy so helpful for patients with chronic joint disorders?

options.A: It provides surgical joint replacement procedures
options.B: It teaches energy-conservation techniques and assistive devices
options.C: It cures the underlying autoimmune malfunction
options.D: It prescribes high-dose corticosteroid injections

explanation: Occupational therapists are wonderful! They teach patients smart ways to protect their joints, save energy, and use handy tools to stay independent. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T12#GNS222_U1_T12_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical healthcare financing challenge in developing countries?

options.A: Large informal economic sectors that evade tax collection
options.B: Excessive government funding that exceeds hospital capacity
options.C: Low budgetary allocation to health by national governments
options.D: High reliance on out-of-pocket payments by patients

question: Which of these is a major duty of the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare?

options.A: Building commercial real estate for private citizens
options.B: Issuing traffic tickets in major cities
options.C: Collecting personal income taxes from workers
options.D: Formulating national health policies and setting clinical standards

question: Which group benefits the most from attending a sheltered workshop?

options.A: Skilled healthcare professionals returning from sabbatical
options.B: Healthy young adults seeking high-paying corporate careers
options.C: Experienced artisans looking for advanced technical training
options.D: Individuals with chronic psychiatric or intellectual disabilities

explanation: These workshops are specially tailored for people whose health challenges make it difficult to jump straight into standard jobs. Keep up the good work! [learn more](GNS314_U5_T7#GNS314_U5_T7_h2)

question: How does a mother's education level usually affect her children's health?

options.A: Educated mothers spend less time taking care of their children at home
options.B: Educated mothers are more likely to understand immunization schedules and hygiene
options.C: Uneducated mothers have better access to modern hospital equipment
options.D: Mothers with schooling rarely experience childhood illnesses in their families

explanation: That's right! Mums who have been to school find it easier to follow health guidelines, leading to better handwashing, timely vaccinations, and healthier kids. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T47#GNS214_U1_T47_h1)

question: Why shouldn't you force a survivor to tell every single detail of their assault right away?

options.A: Forced retelling can trigger severe anxiety and re-traumatize the patient
options.B: Police investigations are always hindered by early patient statements
options.C: Medical records do not need any details about the assault
options.D: Physical examination results become invalid if the patient speaks

explanation: Let survivors take their time. Pressing them to talk too soon can overwhelm them and bring back the trauma. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T13#GNS312_U4_T13_h5)

question: What is the main goal of a Drug Revolving Fund (DRF) in a public hospital?

options.A: To fund free medical care for all citizens indefinitely
options.B: To generate large commercial profits for hospital expansion
options.C: To replace the national health ministry budget entirely
options.D: To guarantee a steady, continuous supply of essential medicines

explanation: Spot on! The whole point of a DRF is to make sure the pharmacy never runs out of crucial drugs by using a self-replenishing pool of money. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T2#GNS215_U3_T2_h1)

question: What do we call the mature, fluid-filled follicle that is fully ready to release an egg?

options.A: Corpus albicans
options.B: Primordial follicle
options.C: Graafian follicle
options.D: Atretic follicle

explanation: The Graafian follicle is the final, mature stage before it bursts open to release the egg. Great landmark to remember in reproductive anatomy! [learn more](GNS121_U5_T7#GNS121_U5_T7_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT one of the five basic tastes?

options.A: Umami
options.B: Salty
options.C: Bitter
options.D: Spicy

explanation: Surprise! Spicy isn't actually a basic chemical taste. That fiery kick you feel is actually your pain and temperature receptors reacting to the pepper! [learn more](GNS311_U3_T1#GNS311_U3_T1_h4)

question: What usually happens when a hospital runs on a strict blame culture?

options.A: Patients experience fewer adverse events during their hospital stay
options.B: Hospital management fixes underlying system problems much faster
options.C: Nurses communicate more openly with physicians about patient care
options.D: Staff hide mistakes and near-misses out of fear of punishment

question: At which stage of behavior change is a person not yet thinking about changing because they see no problem?

options.A: Action
options.B: Preparation
options.C: Maintenance
options.D: Precontemplation

explanation: Think of precontemplation as 'before thinking about it.' The person isn't worried about their habit yet, so change isn't on their mind at all! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h2)

question: In the early days of medicine, what kind of products caused the very first cases of serum sickness?

options.A: Synthetic vitamins
options.B: Purified tap water
options.C: Animal-derived serum
options.D: Plant-based herbal teas

question: How do nurses know how much pain a patient is actually feeling?

options.A: By checking changes in blood pressure
options.B: By measuring the exact amount of tissue damage
options.C: By trusting whatever the patient says it is
options.D: By looking for visible redness and swelling

explanation: You've got this! Pain is entirely personal. Since we can't see or touch it directly, the patient's own word is always our best and most reliable guide. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T7#GNS221_U3_T7_h1)

question: Which hormone acts like a natural relaxant to keep the uterus calm during pregnancy?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Prolactin
options.C: Estrogen
options.D: Progesterone

explanation: Progesterone is the uterus's best friend—it keeps everything calm and relaxed until it's time to meet the baby. Keep up the fantastic work! [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h3)

question: Which patients are usually best suited for progestin-only pills instead of combined pills?

options.A: Patients with a high risk of bacterial skin infections
options.B: Individuals who require permanent surgical sterilization
options.C: Patients suffering from acute iron-deficiency anemia
options.D: Breastfeeding mothers who need to avoid estrogen

explanation: Estrogen can mess with breast milk supply and boost clotting risks. That's why progestin-only options are the go-to safe choice for breastfeeding mums! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T17#GNS215_U6_T17_h4)

question: What is the best nursing trick for a moderate Alzheimer's patient who keeps forgetting to eat full meals?

options.A: Leave a large plate of hot food on the bedside table for hours
options.B: Rely entirely on intravenous fluids for daily nutrition
options.C: Provide frequent nutritious finger foods that are easy to handle
options.D: Insist that the patient sit at the table until the entire plate is empty

explanation: You nailed it! Finger foods make eating much easier for patients who struggle with utensils or lose focus during long meals. Practical nursing at its best! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T2#GNS222_U4_T2_h6)

question: Which of these is a common biological reason for sexual dysfunction in older women?

options.A: Hyperactive thyroid function
options.B: Hormonal shifts during menopause
options.C: Excessive pelvic muscle tone
options.D: Increased production of estrogen

explanation: You've got it! Lower estrogen levels during menopause can cause dryness and tissue changes, which sometimes make things a bit uncomfortable. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T25#GNS312_U1_T25_h4)

question: Why is classifying viruses different from classifying bacteria?

options.A: Viruses lack cellular structure and need a host cell to replicate

options.C: Viruses can be easily stained with standard Gram stain reagents
options.D: Viruses are classified entirely by their ability to form spores

explanation: Because viruses aren't even fully living cells on their own, they hijack human host cells to multiply, making them totally unique to study! [learn more](GST114_U1_T4#GST114_U1_T4_h4)

question: What is the main job of the puborectalis muscle?

options.A: Regulates the flow of urine from the bladder

question: What is a very common psychological cause of male sexual dysfunction?

options.A: Performance anxiety and stress
options.B: High dietary protein consumption
options.C: Regular aerobic exercise
options.D: Excessive daily water intake

explanation: Spot on! The mind plays a huge role; stress, anxiety, and depression can easily get in the way of normal sexual arousal. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T24#GNS312_U1_T24_h4)

question: An angry nursing student wants to yell at a strict clinical instructor, but instead channels that energy into scrubbing the skill lab for hours. What defense mechanism is this?

options.A: Sublimation
options.B: Projection
options.C: Regression
options.D: Denial

explanation: That is sublimation! It is taking raw, unacceptable aggression and turning it into something super productive and socially acceptable. Cleaning counts as a win! [learn more](GNS314_U2_T2#GNS314_U2_T2_h3)

question: How does community health nursing differ from bedside nursing in the hospital?

options.A: It ignores individual patient histories completely
options.B: It requires advanced surgical training for field emergencies
options.C: It deals strictly with paperwork and government health budgets
options.D: It focuses on the collective environment and health of populations

explanation: While bedside nursing cares for one patient at a time, community nursing zooms out to look at whole neighborhoods, environments, and populations! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T9#GNS122_U3_T9_h1)

question: What happens to a patient's digestion when they experience sudden, sharp fear?

options.A: Blood flow to the stomach increases to store energy.
options.B: Digestion slows down sharply as blood is diverted to muscles.
options.C: Digestion speeds up to help process nutrients quickly.
options.D: Acid production stops completely within minutes.

explanation: Exactly! When flight-or-kick mode is activated, the body focuses entirely on survival and moving fast, putting digestion on the back burner. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T11#GNS123_U3_T11_h2)

question: What causes the noisy breathing sound often called the death rattle in a dying patient?

options.A: Accumulation of oral and pharyngeal secretions
options.B: Severe asthma attack in the bronchi
options.C: Swelling of the vocal cords from shouting
options.D: Sudden infection of both lungs

question: Aside from clinical health, what major factor shapes a person's family planning choices?

options.A: Global weather patterns
options.B: Hospital bed capacity

explanation: You nailed it! Family planning choices are deeply tied to cultural traditions, beliefs, and community values, not just pure medicine. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T006#GNS226_U6_T006_h1)

question: What usually blocks the sinuses and triggers a painful sinus infection after a common cold?

options.A: Rupture of the tympanic membrane from high pressure

question: What is an important nursing duty right after a client finishes their EEG?

options.A: Ensuring regular seizure medications are resumed promptly
options.B: Keeping the client awake for another twelve hours

options.D: Applying fresh adhesive paste back onto the scalp

question: What is one key reason for conducting a community diagnosis?

options.C: To eliminate the need for community health workers in rural areas
options.D: To reduce the salaries of local public health administrators

question: How do bad roads and insecurity impact the work of voluntary health agencies?

options.A: They increase the number of qualified volunteer doctors
options.B: They stop community members from falling sick
options.C: They make it difficult to deliver medical supplies safely
options.D: They improve the distribution of government funds

explanation: You got it! Bad roads and security risks make traveling to remote areas a dangerous and stressful chore for healthcare teams. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T28#GNS225_U5_T28_h7)

question: What does fluid balance mean in patient care?

options.A: Fluid intake is greater than output

question: What does an "unmet need" for family planning mean?

options.C: Experiencing side effects from modern oral pills
options.D: Wanting to avoid pregnancy but using no contraception

question: What is a major barrier to price transparency in many healthcare markets?

options.A: Patients are legally barred from asking about expenses
options.B: Hospitals update their price lists every minute
options.C: Final costs are often hidden or unknown until after treatment
options.D: All medical treatments cost the exact same amount globally

question: What does a Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment primarily look at?

options.A: Occupational history and retirement savings

question: What happens when organic matter like blood is left on a surface during disinfection?

question: Why is food safety especially critical for patients with weakened immune systems?

options.A: Their bodies struggle to fight off foodborne infections

options.C: Dirty food automatically stops medicines from working
options.D: Uncooked meat increases muscle mass too fast

question: What information does the 'L' stand for in the SAMPLE history checklist?

question: What does an "out-of-pocket" payment mean in healthcare?

options.D: Direct cash payment made by patients at the point of receiving service

question: What is a vector in the context of disease transmission?

options.A: A living organism, usually an insect, that carries a pathogen to a host
options.B: An open skin lesion that allows bacteria to enter the bloodstream
options.C: A drug resistant bacterial strain found in hospital wards
options.D: A contaminated hospital instrument used on multiple patients

explanation: Vectors are living carriers like mosquitoes, ticks, or fleas that transfer infectious agents from one animal or human to another. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T6#GNS313_U1_T6_h6)

question: What do we call the condition where the foreskin is too tight and cannot be pulled back over the glans?

options.A: Balanitis
options.B: Cryptorchidism
options.C: Phimosis
options.D: Hypospadias

question: A nursing instructor wants students to practice taking a health history and showing empathy to an upset patient. Which simulator type is best suited for this?

question: How should the little prongs of a nasal cannula face when you put them into a patient's nose?

question: Why do pure scare tactics usually fail in teenage drug education programs?

options.C: Young people prefer reading detailed legal textbooks over listening to talks

question: Why do we say food is like medicine when it comes to preventing long-term illnesses?

options.A: Eating specific foods replaces the need for surgical interventions entirely

options.C: Nutrients cure all infectious pathogens without the need for antibiotics

question: What do we call the path germs use to leave their reservoir?

options.B: Susceptible host

options.D: Portal of exit

question: What is the primary cause of Type 1 diabetes mellitus?

options.A: Autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells

question: Which of these is a common natural chemical preservative?

options.B: Artificial nitrate

question: What do we call that difficult time of year right before the new harvest comes in?

options.A: The drought cycle

question: Why are the standard 'rights' of medication administration so important if a legal case of negligence arises?

options.A: They are federal tax requirements for pharmaceutical companies.

question: What does truly comprehensive Post-Abortion Care (PAC) involve beyond treating medical emergencies?

options.A: Restricting her fluid intake to monitor kidney output
options.B: Providing emotional support and linking her to family planning services
options.C: Reporting her to local law enforcement authorities
options.D: Discharging the patient immediately without speaking to her

question: How do you usually arrange the top covers on an admission bed?

options.A: Tucked tightly all around to keep the mattress completely warm

options.C: Arranged in a tight roll directly down the middle of the mattress

question: Why is keeping a close eye on your patient so crucial while moving them in an ambulance?

options.C: Hospital regulations require a full report every sixty seconds

question: What is a common misconception about mental illness in many Nigerian communities?

question: Why might a newly graduated nurse hesitate to accept delegated duties from a senior colleague?

question: Why are iron supplements routinely given during antenatal care?

question: What do we call a close call in the clinical area where a mistake almost happens?

question: Which hormone is mainly responsible for the breathing changes you see in a pregnant woman?

question: What causes 'goosebumps' on your skin when you feel cold or frightened?

question: Why is depression in an older adult considered a condition requiring treatment rather than a normal part of aging?

question: What is the primary cellular deficit in Parkinson's disease?

question: Which of these duties should a registered nurse NEVER delegate to an untrained ward assistant?

question: Which of the following is NOT a common challenge faced in community health planning in Nigeria?

question: A healthy family member who was exposed to measles is asked to stay at home and avoid contact with others for a short period. What is this control measure called?

question: Why do family caregivers often get so stressed or upset when a sick patient refuses to eat?

question: Which food item is best suited for adding hidden calories to a bowl of porridge?

question: What is the best nursing action when you spot a potential drug interaction on a patient's chart?

question: How do a person's cultural and spiritual beliefs usually affect how they grieve?

question: Why do clients with inherited degenerative disorders need a team of different specialists (multidisciplinary team)?

question: Why do many pregnant women notice dark skin patches like the linea nigra on their belly?

question: What exactly is caregiver burnout?

question: Which common side effect often occurs due to the stimulant properties of bronchodilators like albuterol?

question: Why are some oral tablets manufactured with an enteric coating?

question: What is the primary hormone responsible for moving glucose from the bloodstream into body cells?

question: At what age should complementary foods be introduced to an infant?

question: How does keeping track of a patient's starting diet help the healthcare team?

options.C: 210 mg/dL
options.D: 55 mg/dL

question: Why do nurse researchers check their ideas against the FINER criteria before starting a study?

options.A: To check if the study is practical, ethical, and worth doing
options.B: To calculate the exact sample size needed for data analysis
options.C: To write the discussion section of the research paper
options.D: To select the statistical software for data entry

explanation: FINER (Feasible, Interesting, Novel, Ethical, Relevant) acts like a safety check to make sure your study idea is worth your time and safe for patients. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T8#GNS217_U3_T8_h4)

question: What does a high PaCO2 level on an arterial blood gas (ABG) report usually tell you?

options.A: Inadequate ventilation or carbon dioxide retention
options.B: Excessive bicarbonate production by the liver
options.C: Too much oxygen being delivered by the ventilator
options.D: Rapid breathing caused by severe emotional anxiety

explanation: If the lungs aren't blowing off air well enough, carbon dioxide builds up in the blood, driving that PaCO2 level right up. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h3)

question: When does a patient maintain a stable body weight?

options.A: Energy intake equals energy expenditure
options.B: Energy intake drops to zero for a day
options.C: Energy intake exceeds energy expenditure
options.D: Energy expenditure is higher than energy intake

explanation: Weight remains stable when the total calories consumed match the total calories burned by the body. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h1)

question: Which physical reaction does the hypothalamus trigger during a fight-or-flight response?

options.A: Increased digestion
options.B: Increased heart rate
options.C: Narrowed airways
options.D: Slower breathing

explanation: Spot on! Stress hormones released via the hypothalamus make your heart beat faster to pump extra oxygen and blood to your muscles. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T13#GNS211_U3_T13_h5)

question: Why is it so important to tell a patient to cough up deep lung mucus instead of just spitting out mouth saliva for a TB test?

options.A: Deep-lung samples prevent the patient from coughing blood
options.B: Saliva damages the expensive laboratory testing equipment
options.C: Saliva does not contain the actual bacteria from the lungs
options.D: Saliva samples take much longer to process in the lab

explanation: Makes total sense, right? TB lives deep in the lungs, so mouth saliva won't show us the bacteria we need to find for an accurate diagnosis. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T96#GNS214_U1_T96_h4)

question: A patient complains of sharp pain in their lower right tummy. Which organ should a nurse suspect right away?

options.A: Spleen
options.B: Stomach
options.C: Heart
options.D: Appendix

explanation: Classic clinical scenario! The appendix is typically tucked away in the lower right quarter of the abdomen. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T3#GNS111_U1_T3_h6)

question: Why might a multi-million-dollar MRI machine be considered inappropriate technology for a rural primary health clinic?

options.A: Rural patients do not have brains or spinal cords to scan
options.B: Magnetic machines are forbidden by traditional cultural beliefs
options.C: The clinic lacks reliable electricity, trained technicians, and repair parts
options.D: The government prefers traditional herbs over digital imaging

explanation: Advanced machinery fails the test of appropriateness if the local setting lacks the infrastructure and support to keep it running. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h6)

question: Why is teaching patients to read food labels a great nursing skill for fat management?

options.A: It proves processed foods are dangerous
options.B: It helps them spot hidden trans and saturated fats
options.C: It guarantees quick weight loss
options.D: It means they never need to see a dietitian again

explanation: Food labels can be tricky! Teaching patients to read them empowers them to catch hidden bad fats lurking in packaged snacks. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T011#GNS227_U4_T011_h5)

question: What is the primary goal of a post-disaster debriefing or hot wash session?

options.A: Calculating annual bonuses for hospital administrators
options.B: Analyzing what went well and where emergency processes failed
options.C: Assigning blame to individual nurses who made mistakes
options.D: Destroying all medical records from the disaster period

explanation: Debriefings review the response objectively so the healthcare team can learn and improve for future emergencies. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T2#GNS315_U5_T2_h8)

question: Why should a nurse check the patient's manual pulse against the pulse rate displayed on the oximeter?

options.A: To clean any dust off the infrared sensor window
options.B: To calibrate the battery level inside the monitor casing
options.C: To confirm the machine is accurately detecting the pulse signal
options.D: To make sure the patient's blood pressure is normal

explanation: Comparing heart rates ensures the oximeter is picking up a true pulse rather than background motion artifacts or weak signals. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T6#GNS212_U4_T6_h6)

question: Why is routine screening for high blood pressure classified as secondary prevention?

options.A: It completely prevents a person from ever developing hypertension
options.B: It is only performed after a patient has suffered a major stroke
options.C: It catches an existing condition early before severe complications develop
options.D: It focuses purely on physical rehabilitation in a hospital ward

explanation: Secondary prevention focuses on early diagnosis and screening so treatment can start early. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T5#GNS123_U1_T5_h4)
